title: Shrink the image
summary: A small Flask app ships in a container image of more than 1 GB that runs as root. Rewrite the Dockerfile so the image is under 200 MB, runs as a normal user and still works.

checks.name: The image builds
checks.description: docker build finishes within 10 minutes on a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner. A # syntax= line may only name docker/dockerfile.

checks.name: Under 200 MB
checks.description: The image is at most 200 MB (200,000,000 bytes), as docker image inspect reports it.

checks.name: Runs as a non-root user
checks.description: The image sets a USER that is not root, and no process in the running container has UID 0.

checks.name: Starts and answers /health
checks.description: The container, started with no extra arguments, answers GET /health on port 8000 with HTTP 200 within 20 seconds.

checks.name: The app still works
checks.description: GET /slugify?text=... returns the right slug for a random text, so the image runs the real app.
